newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS BEAT BRUINS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS BEAT BRUINS.

text.p: John MacLean had two goals and and Dave Andreychuk and Denis Pederson each had a goal to lead the New Jersey Devils to their first win in Boston in nearly three years, 7-4 over the Bruins on Thursday.
Valeri Zelepukin contributed three assists for the Devils.
"That's the type of game I love, the seven goals part," said Devils coach Jacques Lemaire. "I didn't like that we gave four, though. I guess we just can't relax."
In Detroit, Brendan Shanahan had a goal and two assists and Sergei Fedorov and Steve Yzerman each added a goal and an assist as the Detroit Red Wings beat the Chicago Blackhawks, 6-2.

After the Blackhawks took a 2-0 lead into the first intermission, the Red Wings stormed back to score the next six goals, peppering Chicago goaltender Ed Belfour with 33 shots in the final two periods.

In Philadelphia, Eric Lindros and John LeClair scored in a 2:14 span of the second period and the Philadelphia Flyers extended their unbeaten streak to six games by holding on for a 3-2 victory over the Hartford Whalers in the opener of a home-and-home series.
Pat Falloon had the other goal for Philadelphia. The Flyers also continued their dominance over Hartford, improving to 12-2-1 in their last 15 meetings.
Philadelphia outshot the Whalers in the second period, 20-5, and had a 30-19 edge for the game.
At Tampa Bay, Roman Hamrlik scored 57 seconds into the third period to lift the Tampa Bay Lightning to a 2-2 tie with the Edmonton Oilers.
With the Lightning on a power play, Hamrlik took a pass from David Shaw at the right point and put a slap shot over goaltender Curtis Joseph's glove for his fourth goal.
"That's as hard a fought point as we've gotten," said Tampa Bay coach Terry Crisp. "Again we had so many scoring opportunities and couldn't put it away."

In Los Angeles, Dwayne Roloson stopped 35 shots and rookie Jarome Iginla and Cory Stillman each had a goal and an assist as the Calgary Flames won for just the second time in three weeks, defeating the Los Angeles Kings, 5-1.
The Flames got goals from five different players.
Iginla scored for the third time in his last four games.
